To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the best results for entity list completion can be achieved by a combination of a cluster-based context representation and the use of the list description as query, while the best results for the entity ranking task can be achieved by the use of a cluster-based representation of both the query and the entity.

(i) for entity list completion, the use of cluster-based contexts leads to a substantial performance improvement, and (ii) for entity ranking, the use of entity descriptions as input leads to a substantial improvement over the use of entity titles.
(a) for entity ranking, the use of a cluster-based context representation improves results, and (b) for list completion, the use of an example-based context representation improves retrieval results.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: (1) Can entity retrieval algorithms be applied to list completion and entity search tasks, and if so, how can they be adapted to these tasks?

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose and evaluate a set of algorithms to address two new entity retrieval tasks.

the best results are obtained when combining the two tasks, i.e. when using the entity ranking task to select the most relevant entities and using the entity ranking results for the list completion task.
we propose and evaluate two new tasks for entity retrieval, and we propose and evaluate new representations for entities that improve results for the two tasks.
